Preprint — arXiv:2609.36319v1 [cs.AI], 28 Sep 2026 (pages headed 'Preprint'); no published venue found (no journal_ref in the arXiv export, not in the other exports)
Causal Dynamics Lab; Emory University (Yu, Zhao)

Proposes an approach; secondary: Proposes an evaluation method — StateTape, write-conditioned context maintenance for coding agents via a symbol-level code graph, a tape of graph diffs and a small manager model; plus TraceBench, a benchmark of held vs needed context. Includes a theoretical analysis and a comparison with Control and four baselines

StateTape (authors' own, no version). Baselines in the same shim: Control (unmodified agent), observation masking, LLM summary (Lindenbauer et al. 2025 settings), CORVUS, text-only manager in AgentDiet style

Symbol-level code graph (symbols, call edges, bodies) updated at every write; tape logging drifted symbols per write; context records (text, referent, step); manager actions REFRESH / DROP (tombstone) / RERUN (stub) / KEEP; nine read-only manager skills. No specification artefact

Per write: tape applies write to code graph -> computes drifted symbols (body changes and call-edge changes) -> nominates held records covering drifted symbols (no model call) -> manager (small LLM) decides REFRESH/DROP/RERUN/KEEP, evicts finished records, retrieves code up to two call hops from drifted symbols -> next agent request carries maintained context (Fig. 4)
None (fully automatic; TraceBench human review queue built but not yet filled)

Tasks: three edit-heavy benchmarks + TraceBench (403 decision points from Claude Code + Opus 4.8 on 48 SWE-EVO instances). Configurations: 6 agent+model x {Control, 4 baselines, StateTape} = 108 cells + 3 ablations. Baseline: Control (unmodified agent). Held constant: agent, model, shim, Docker container, 90-min limit (30 min per SlopCodeBench checkpoint), no turn limit, single Apple M5 Pro host. Acceptance: benchmark tests. Repetitions: Not stated (apparently one run per cell). Human intervention: none

StateTape best in all 18 agent-benchmark cells; mean gain over Control +4.9 (SWE-EVO), +2.7 (SlopCode), +3.3 (SWE-Pro); Sonnet 5 gains most (6.2, 3.6, 4.9). Manager tokens 2.6% of agent tokens overall. Highest CE (6.18) and RE (10.47) on TraceBench. Ablation: removing code graph -3.37, tape -3.07, manager -1.97 points mean. No significance testing reported

Distinguished StateTape from baselines consistently in direction, but differences are a few points with no variance, repetitions or significance reported; the SWE-EVO end-to-end instance count is not stated, though all SWE-EVO values are multiples of 1/48 (2.08 points), which suggests 48 instances, i.e. about one instance per 2.1 points (extractor's inference). Authors note resolve rate is a loose one-bit-per-instance signal that moves 'by a few points', motivating TraceBench. TraceBench limitations: silver labels (LLM judge, human review queue not yet filled), one agent on one suite, base rates may not transfer, gold relative to the reference patch

No limitations section in the main paper. Appendix E: TraceBench labels silver, one agent/one suite, base rates may not transfer to other scaffolds, gold context relative to the reference patch. Theorem 1 holds under a symbol-locality assumption
